claims.statement: The standard cat map has one binary length-three orbit; the split, inert, and ramified formulas stated in Theorem 2.1 hold; p=2 is the unique one-orbit prime shell and m_p>=p-1 for every odd prime.
claims.boundary: Classical orbit arithmetic is re-derived, not claimed as new; no maximal-order assumption is used.

claims.statement: The point-potential return product is product_gamma (1-p^(-s|gamma|))^(-1), whereas the one-time orbit-label product is (1-p^(-s))^(-m_p) with repeat coefficient m_p/r.
claims.boundary: The two constructions are never identified; no numerical s or logarithm is evaluated.

claims.statement: For an odd prime, a finite pure denominator with fixed nonzero scalar coefficients independent of z cannot equal one factor (1-z)^(-1); with zeros equality requires weights {1,0,...,0}.
claims.boundary: Does not cover matrix-valued, z-dependent, numerator, alternating, Fredholm, transfer, or cohomological constructions.

claims.statement: Equal weights 1/m_p repair only the first power sum when m_p>1.
claims.boundary: Registered r=1,2,3 values are examples of the exact identity, not an infinite numerical test.

claims.statement: Fractional outer exponents |gamma|/(p^2-1) give exactly one prime-shell factor and the same normalized partition identity extends symbolically to exact-order composite shells via J_2(q).
claims.boundary: This is global normalized counting, not an ordinary scalar weight; no composite shell was selected or enumerated.

claims.statement: A one-orbit selector produces one factor but discards exactly m_p-1 cycles.
claims.boundary: No impossibility of an enriched or canonical selector is claimed.

claims.statement: The global label logarithm diverges for real 1<s<=2, is not absolutely convergent for complex 1<Re(s)<=2, and is absolutely convergent for Re(s)>3.
claims.boundary: No claim for 2<Re(s)<=3, exact abscissa, conditional convergence, continuation, functional equation, or zeros.

claims.statement: The one registered development-seen audit at p={2,3,5,7,11} reproduced m_p={1,2,4,6,24}, 203 nonzero points, 37 cycles, and 12 of 12 exact controls by two implementations.
claims.boundary: Finite falsification control only; it is not all-prime or analytic evidence.

claims.statement: Centralizer quotients and matrix, numerator, alternating, Fredholm, transfer, and cohomological mechanisms remain genuine outside-theorem escapes.
claims.boundary: The present audit neither constructs nor rules out these routes; centralizer work was not run.
